Diagnosis:
The test case `testRoundTripNames()` calls `checkName` with various strings, including one with special characters outside the ASCII 0-127 range, specifically the string "0302-0601-3±±±F06±W220±ZB±LALALA±±±±±±±±±±CAN±±DC±±±04±060302±MOE.model". The current bug report states that `TarUtils.parseName` does not properly handle characters outside the range 0-127 and shows that special characters like '±' are incorrectly decoded to other characters.

Reviewing the code of `TarUtils.parseName(byte[], int, int)`, the method converts each byte in the specified range to a char by simple casting: `result.append((char) buffer[i]);`. This direct cast from byte to char does not correctly interpret bytes representing characters with values greater than 127. In Java, bytes are signed (values from -128 to 127), and casting to char directly results in incorrect character interpretation for negative byte values (which represent unsigned values > 127). Thus, special characters are misrepresented in the resulting String.

The bug report suggests a fix: instead of casting the byte to char directly, construct a `String` using `new String(new byte[] { buffer[i] })` which properly interprets the byte as a single-character string in the platform's default character encoding.

The root cause is the improper casting of bytes to chars without handling encoding, leading to incorrect names when special (non-ASCII) characters are present in the tar entry names.

None of the recent bug reports appears relevant to this issue since they concern SHA1 file formatting, ZIP data descriptors, and recognition of tar files created by Ant.

Hence, the bug is in `TarUtils.parseName` which should be changed to properly convert bytes to characters (likely by using `new String(byte[], offset, length, Charset)` or by appending `new String(new byte[] { buffer[i] })` instead of casting bytes directly to char.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
